title: The 4 Pillars of Object-Oriented Programming
intro: OOP shows up in interviews and in languages like Java, Python and C#. Here are the four core ideas in plain words.

slides.heading: Encapsulation
slides.subtitle: Keep data and behavior together.
points: Bundle data with the methods that use it
Hide internal details behind a clear interface

slides.heading: Abstraction
slides.subtitle: Show only what matters.
points: Expose simple methods, hide the complexity
Like driving a car without knowing the engine

slides.heading: Inheritance
slides.subtitle: Reuse code from a parent class.
points: A child class extends a parent class
Use it only for true "is-a" relationships

slides.heading: Polymorphism
slides.subtitle: One interface, many forms.
points: Different classes answer the same method
Code works with any object that fits

scenario.situation: A payment app supports cards and now needs UPI and PayPal too.
scenario.problem: One giant function with an if/else for every payment type gets harder to change with each new method.
scenario.fix: Create a Payment interface with pay(). Card, UPI and PayPal each implement it, and checkout just calls pay().
scenario.takeaway: Polymorphism lets you add new types without editing old code.

cta: Which pillar was hardest to understand at first?
